title: How this site is built
lead: The site is a small version of the architecture I've worked with: a Next.js shell that loads independently built Module Federation remotes, with typed content, typed contracts and CI on every push. It is fully static, so it costs nothing to host.

decisions.title: A runtime federation host instead of a build plugin
decisions.body: Next.js App Router has no supported Module Federation build plugin, so the shell is a runtime host. Each remote is built by webpack with @module-federation/enhanced, and the shell loads the containers in the browser with @module-federation/runtime.

decisions.title: One React, provided by the shell
decisions.body: Remotes declare React as a shared singleton with import: false, so they can't bundle their own copy. Hooks and context work across the boundary, and each remote ships only its own code.

decisions.title: Failures stay inside their box
decisions.body: Every remote mounts inside a boundary that handles both a failed network load and a crash during render, with a contained fallback and a retry. The case-study charts run this way.

decisions.title: Typed contracts at the boundary
decisions.body: Props for every exposed module live in a shared contracts package. Both the shell and the remotes compile against it, so a breaking prop change fails typecheck on both sides.

decisions.title: Content is data, validated at build
decisions.body: Copy, metrics, projects and company pages are JSON validated with Zod when the site builds. Broken cross-references and illustrative numbers that drift from the verified ones stop the build.

decisions.title: Recruiter mode without a server
decisions.body: Skim and deep-dive modes are a data attribute on <html>, set before first paint from localStorage or ?mode=. CSS shows or hides sections, so pages stay static and search engines see everything.

decisions.title: Static export, free hosting
decisions.body: next build produces plain HTML, JS and CSS with the remotes copied alongside. It deploys to Vercel's free tier or GitHub Pages with no server to run.

quality: TypeScript strict across every package, including noUncheckedIndexedAccess.
Jest and React Testing Library for logic and components; Playwright for end-to-end flows and axe accessibility checks.
GitHub Actions runs lint, typecheck, unit tests, build and end-to-end tests on every push.
Semantic HTML, keyboard support throughout, visible focus, reduced-motion support and WCAG AA contrast in both themes.
